title: Pressure Cooker Ki Seeti Kyun Bajti Hai?

lines.spoken: روز ایسی ایک نئی بات کے لیے، فالو کریں۔

fact_notes: At sea level water boils at 100 C in an open pot; extra heat only turns more water into steam, so the water temperature stays at about 100 C.
A pressure cooker's lid is sealed by a rubber gasket, so steam is trapped and the pressure rises; typical cookers run at about 15 psi (~1 bar) above atmospheric, where water boils at about 120-121 C.
The higher temperature cooks food much faster; cooking times drop to roughly a third or less (2-3x faster is a conservative claim).

The whistle on South Asian cookers is a weighted pressure regulator sitting on the vent pipe: when pressure exceeds the set point, steam lifts the weight, escapes with a whistle, and the weight drops back; it releases excess pressure (cookers also have a separate safety valve/plug).
